New medical reports submitted by the worker in this case did not meet that standard.

DecSummary: The worker suffered a compensable injury in 1990. He was granted a full FEL award at D1. By R1, the worker was receiving CPP disability benefits. At R1 and R2, the Board granted a full FEL award but the award was offset by the amount of the CPP disability benefits. Section 44(1) of the pre-1997 Act requires the Board to set aside additional funds for a retirement pension for the worker in an amount equal to 10% of every payment made to the worker under s. 43. Starting at R1, the Board set aside 10% of the actual dollar amount paid to the worker, as offset by the CPP disability benefits. In Decision No. 1878/04, the vice-chair allowed the worker's appeal and found that the 10% set aside for the retirement pension should be 10% of the amount that reflected the Board's initial determination of the worker's likely future loss of earnings without any offset of CPP benefits.
